# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I should not act yet. I need Deaf to tell me what's printed (colours/markings) and Mute to relay the manual rules, since I can only hear Mute and only gesture to Deaf/Mute. But at turn 1, Deaf hasn't spoken yet (order is Mute, Blind, Deaf), so I've heard nothing from anyone this round.

Best move: gesture to Deaf that I'm ready and need their visual description, and speak to Mute asking them to relay anything relevant from the manual. Keep it minimal since I have no data.

Actually, careful: I never receive gesture, and I receive speech only from Mute (who comes before me). Deaf comes after me, so Deaf's turn-1 message reaches me at start of turn 2. So right now I truly have nothing.

I'll send a short ready-signal and a request, then wait for input.

speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, hands empty, nothing felt yet. Please relay any manual rule about wires 1-3 and how display/light map to them. I will wait for Deaf's description before acting.")

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light changed again to yellow — the sequence has looped. Full repeating cycle: yellow, blue, white, red, purple, then back to yellow. Five colors cycling. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. What does the manual say?

Deaf reports the light cycles through five colours: yellow, blue, white, red, purple, then loops. Display 0. Wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Still nothing from Mute.

Let me think hard, because Mute may never speak and I may have to reason from what I have.

Facts:
- Light cycles through 5 colours: yellow, blue, white, red, purple.
- Display reads 0.
- Wires: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.
- I have no manual rule.

Deaf's earlier observation: blue and red appear in the light; green does not. In the cycle {yellow, blue, white, red, purple}, the wire colours present are blue and red; green is absent. That's a clean discriminator: wire 3 (green) is the only wire colour NOT in the light cycle. A plausible rule: cut the wire whose colour never appears in the light.

But this is a guess without the manual. The rules say a wrong action detonates. I have no confirmation.

However — I should weigh this. Mute has been silent for 7 rounds. If Mute never speaks, waiting forever means never defusing. But the puzzle likely expects Mute to eventually relay the rule. Still, I cannot invent a rule.

Let me reconsider the display: it reads 0. Maybe display 0 means something like "cut position 1"? Or display counts something? With no manual, 0 is ambiguous.

Given the strong, clean signal (green is the only wire colour absent from the light cycle), this is the most likely intended rule. But I should not act on an unconfirmed guess. I'll relay to Mute one final time, explicitly stating my hypothesis and asking for confirmation. If Mute confirms, I cut wire 3.

Actually, I should also gesture to Deaf the hypothesis so Deaf can sanity-check against anything printed on the bomb (Deaf sees all markings). Deaf might see a legend or marking that confirms.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light cycles five colours: yellow, blue, white, red, purple. Display 0. Wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Hypothesis: cut the wire whose colour never appears in the light cycle — that is wire 3, green. Confirm from the manual.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👌", "👉", "👆", "🖐"])

```

The rules: a wrong action detonates. There is no second attempt. So acting on a guess is dangerous. But Mute is the only source of the manual, and Mute has never spoken. Either Mute is stuck, or Mute's channel to me is broken.

But I'm wary. Let me consider alternatives:
- Display 0 could mean cut position is derived from display. 0 → maybe position 1? Or "0" means no cut / already set?
- The rule might be "cut the wire matching the current light colour" — but light changes, so that'd be unstable. At this moment light is blue → wire 1. That's also plausible and simpler.

Hmm. Two competing simple rules:
1. Cut the wire whose colour never appears in the light cycle → wire 3 (green).
2. Cut the wire matching the current light colour → wire 1 (blue) right now.

Rule 2 is unstable (light keeps changing), which is odd for a puzzle. Rule 1 is stable and uses the full cycle information, which the puzzle has been feeding us deliberately (Deaf reported the whole loop). The design strongly suggests rule 1: the light cycles to reveal the set of colours, and the answer is the wire colour excluded from that set.

Also note: the light cycle has 5 colours, wires have 3. The intersection is {blue, red}. The complement in wire colours is {green}. This is an elegant, deliberate construction.

I'll commit to wire 3. But before acting, I should make one last attempt to get Mute, and I should tell Deaf my decision so the record is clear. Actually, acting is my call alone. I'll state my reasoning, then cut position 3.

Wait — I should be careful. Let me not rush. Is there any chance the answer is wire 1 or 2? The cleanest discriminator is green's absence. I'll go with position 3.

Let me also send a final message to Mute stating I'm proceeding, and gesture to Deaf. Then act.

Actually, the instruction says calls are literal and the program decides. I'll include the act call. Let me put speak, gesture, then act.
